turns.user: Design a low-carbon grout paste: mini-slump flow diameter >= 200 mm and 7-day compressive strength >= 30 MPa, minimise CO2. Space: w/b 0.30-0.50, OPC required, class F fly ash 0-0.5. Run without asking.
turns.text:
I’ll run the inverse design now using the stated bounds, treating this as a paste/grout system and minimizing embodied CO₂ subject to both performance constraints. I’ll report all defaults applied, uncertainty, range violations, and the generated file paths.
The optimization is still refining candidates. The flow constraint uses the weak mini-slump model with a deliberately lower feasibility-probability threshold, while 7-day strength uses the stronger threshold; published analogue mixes will remain the primary evidence for flow.
Recommended lowest-CO₂ feasible candidate:

- Paste binder: OPC 71%, class F fly ash 29%
- w/b: 0.307
- Estimated CO₂: 908.079 kg/m³
- Mini-slump: 191.4 [91.9, 292.0] mm; probability of ≥200 mm: 0.46
- 7-day compressive strength: 33.3 [23.1, 59.7] MPa; probability of ≥30 MPa: 0.66
- Joint feasibility probability: 0.301

The mini-slump model is weak (R²log = −0.178), so its result is only order-of-magnitude guidance. Primary supporting evidence is an OPC–class F fly ash paste containing 15% fly ash, w/b 0.30, and 0.50% PCE, experimentally achieving 268 mm flow and 82 MPa at 7 days ([DOI](https://doi.org/10.3389/fmats.2021.712551)). PCE was not included in your search space.

Defaults: paste system, moist curing at 20 °C and 95% RH, 50-mm compression cube, non-3DCP model; no sand or admixture was specified. Experimental verification is required, particularly for flow.
